answers.answer: Factory deck is placed on the Factory territory and encounter tokens are placed on designated territories. Setup of structure bonus tiles and starting player is not stated.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Place encounter tokens on designated territories. Place the Factory card deck on the Factory territory.” Final Scoring mentions “structure bonus tile coins (varies)” but not setup.

answers.answer: The summary says characters start on faction home bases and one worker on each adjacent territory; combat power and popularity markers start at faction-dependent positions. Starting combat cards, coins, and objective cards are received as indicated, but it does not say which mat provides each. Other starting map pieces and mat contents are not specified.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Place the character on the faction's home base and one worker on each adjacent territory. Set combat power and popularity markers at starting positions (varies by Faction mat). Receive starting combat cards, coins, and objective cards as indicated.”

answers.answer: You may take one action, both, or neither, but must move the token. A section cannot be repeated from the previous turn, except the summary notes the Rusviet exception. The summary does not say whether top-row gains can pay bottom-row costs, whether bottom action may come first, or how costs and benefits are calculated beyond “pay cost, gain benefit.”
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “You may take one action, both, or neither, but you must move your token.” It also says “cannot repeat the same section as your previous turn” and names the Rusviet exception.

answers.answer: The summary says resources belong to whoever controls a territory. It does not specify control of a structure territory occupied by an enemy worker, who may use a structure, or the locations from which resources may be spent for an action elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: “Resource Ownership: Resources on a territory belong to whoever controls that territory.”

answers.answer: A normal Move moves up to two units one territory each, so whether one unit can move twice is not specified. The summary does not state whether transported workers can subsequently move or the detailed carrying restrictions; it only says mechs can carry workers and workers carry resources.
answers.evidence: Move: “Move up to 2 units (character, worker, or mech) one territory each.” “Mechs can carry workers. Workers carry resources.”

answers.answer: The summary says moving into a territory with opponent workers forces them to retreat and costs one popularity per retreating worker. It does not specify Speed-enabled entry or whether the mech's workers may enter alone, including at zero popularity.
answers.evidence: Move: “Moving into a territory with opponent workers forces them to retreat (lose 1 popularity per retreating worker).” Speed is only listed as a mech ability.

answers.answer: Combat occurs when character/mechs share a territory with opponent character/mechs after movement. Multiple combat order and whether workers can enter or leave an enemy character/mech-controlled territory alone are not stated. The summary says workers cannot initiate combat; only characters and mechs fight.
answers.evidence: Combat: “When your character/mechs share a territory with opponent character/mechs after movement.” Special Rules: “Workers cannot initiate combat. Only characters and mechs fight.”

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives a choice of 2 Power or 1 Combat Card. Trade costs $1 and gives 2 chosen resources on territories you control with workers, or 1 Popularity. The all-workers-home case and what happens if the combat deck is exhausted are not stated.
answers.evidence: Top-Row Actions: “Bolster (pay $1): Gain 2 Power ... OR draw 1 Combat Card.” “Trade (pay $1): Gain 2 resources ... on territories you control with workers, OR gain 1 Popularity.”

answers.answer: Produce has a variable cost; you choose up to two territories you control with workers, and workers there produce one terrain-matching resource each (a Village produces a worker). The summary does not explain how the cost is paid, where new workers come from, whether benefits may be declined, or whether new workers affect an already-paid cost.
answers.evidence: Produce: “pay variable cost”; “Choose up to 2 territories you control with workers. Each worker on those territories produces 1 resource matching the terrain ... Village = Worker.”

answers.answer: Upgrade costs Oil and moves a technology cube from a green top-row box to a red bottom-row box, improving action efficiency. Deploy costs Metal and places a mech on a territory with workers, unlocking a faction-specific ability for the character and all mechs. Exact costs, further placement restrictions, and whether a completed bottom action can still be paid are not given.
answers.evidence: Bottom-Row Actions: “Upgrade (pay Oil)” and “Deploy (pay Metal): Place a mech on a territory with workers.”

answers.answer: Build costs Wood and places a structure on a territory with workers, with at most one structure per territory. No rule is given on moving or destroying structures, or how Mill/Mine function when enemy units occupy their territories. The Mill counts as an extra territory for Produce; Mine acts as a personal tunnel adjacent to other tunnels.
answers.evidence: Build: “Place a structure on a territory with workers (max 1 structure per territory).” Mill and Mine effects are listed in Bottom-Row Actions.

answers.answer: Enlist costs Food and places a recruit token, with a one-time bonus of 2 Power, 2 Coins, 2 Popularity, or 2 Combat Cards. Ongoing bonus is received whenever you or adjacent players take that bottom-row action. The summary does not specify token placement location, how the action setting is determined, or simultaneous/two-player bonus resolution.
answers.evidence: Enlist: “Place a recruit token, gaining a one-time bonus (2 Power, 2 Coins, 2 Popularity, or 2 Combat Cards). Ongoing bonus: Gain the specified bonus whenever you OR adjacent players take that bottom-row action.”

answers.answer: Each player secretly selects dial power from 0 to current power and may add up to one combat card per unit involved; reveal simultaneously, and highest total wins with attacker winning ties. Combat-ability resolution and how totals are paid are not detailed.
answers.evidence: Combat: “Both players secretly select power on their dial (0 to current power). Each player may add up to 1 combat card per unit involved. Reveal simultaneously. Highest total wins (attacker wins ties).”

answers.answer: Winner stays, keeps resources, and places a combat star. Loser retreats all units to home base and gains one combat card if they committed any power. The summary does not specify popularity changes after combat or any other resource handling beyond the winner keeping resources.
answers.evidence: Combat: “Winner: Stays on territory, keeps resources, places combat star. Loser: Retreats all units to home base, gains 1 combat card if they committed any power.”

answers.answer: Moving the character onto an encounter token triggers an encounter after all movement/combat. The summary does not explain contested-entry timing or what happens if the character loses. It says to draw a card with three options and choose one; the exact destination of gains and whether normal action costs/bonuses apply are unstated.
answers.evidence: Move: “Moving character onto an encounter token triggers an encounter after all movement/combat.” Special Rules: “draw a card with three options. Choose one (gain resources, popularity, power, etc.).”

answers.answer: The first character to reach the Factory gains a Factory card providing a fifth action section. The summary does not say when during a turn this happens, whether later visitors may take cards or change theirs, or how Factory actions and Speed movement differ from mat actions.
answers.evidence: Factory: “The first character to reach the Factory gains a Factory card providing a 5th action section on their Player mat.”

answers.answer: The summary says a completed Objective Card can earn a star, but does not state when it may be revealed, its requirements, what must be discarded, or any Saxony-specific change.
answers.evidence: Star Placement: “Reveal a completed Objective Card.” No further objective rules are summarized.

answers.answer: Listed star achievements are completing 6 upgrades, deploying 4 mechs, building 4 structures, enlisting 4 recruits, placing 8 workers, revealing a completed objective, winning combat (max 2 stars except Saxony unlimited), reaching 18 Popularity, and reaching 16 Power. Whether stars can be lost or another player can block a goal is not stated. Game ends immediately when any player places a sixth star.
answers.evidence: Star Placement lists these achievements and limits; Game End Trigger: “The game ends immediately when any player places their 6th star on the Triumph Track.”

answers.answer: The summary does not specify what is collected before a sixth star earned by a bottom action, how pending battles are handled, or whether a neighboring recruit bonus star is resolved.
answers.evidence: The summary states only that the game ends immediately when a player places their sixth star; it gives no sequencing for these events.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, the summary's tier table puts the player in Tier 2 (7–12). The stated additions are 4 coins per star (5 stars = 20), 3 per territory (4 normal territories plus Factory = 15), and 2 per 2 resources; 13 resources would yield 6 complete pairs for 12 coins, with handling of the leftover resource unstated. Sum of stated amounts: 47 coins added to held coins, before any structure bonus. Structure bonus eligibility and all victory tiebreakers are not stated; the summary only says bonus tile coins vary and the player with most total coins wins.
answers.evidence: Final Scoring: popularity tiers 7–12 are Tier 2; table gives $4 per star, $3 per territory, $2 per 2 resources. It adds “Plus structure bonus tile coins (varies)” and says most total coins wins.
